pipelineStages.system: HE (University) source system via REST API; or Excel/portal upload bridge for exception-approved institutions; legacy School System Portal remains for existing users (read-only reference in our portal)
pipelineStages.whatPortalShows: Submission card header: institution, dataset, reporting period, channel (API | portal upload), dictionary version targeted, initiated-by user or client ID, row count, payload/file hash, submitted-at, correlation ID. For portal-upload channel: Steward draft, upload result (rows accepted / skipped duplicates / flagged), Approver sign-off before dispatch. For API channel: the client ID and environment (sandbox | production) that sent it.

pipelineStages.system: iPaaS integration layer - secure API access: auth, client ID, secret, private/public key, IP whitelisting
pipelineStages.whatPortalShows: Journey step 'Received by integration layer': received-at timestamp, client ID used, auth method (secret | key pair), signature check result, source IP and whether it matched an allowlist entry, correlation ID, forwarded-at. On failure: reason code (invalid_client, bad_signature, ip_not_allowed) with a 'fix it' link to the credential or allowlist page. Aggregated on KHDA IT Integration Health: auth success rate, rejected-by-IP count, per-institution last successful call.

pipelineStages.system: Azure API Management - inbound/outbound validation: auth validation, token validation, IP whitelisting, throttling, contract check
pipelineStages.whatPortalShows: Journey step 'Gateway validation': token validated (issued-at / expires-at, token ID), IP check result, API product/version invoked, request ID, latency ms, HTTP status, rate-limit state. On failure: token_expired, token_invalid, ip_rejected, throttled, contract_mismatch with the returned error body. KHDA IT view: gateway health per environment, throttle events, token issuance timeline, error-code breakdown; institution view: their own recent gateway calls (self-service diagnostics).

pipelineStages.system: University Adapter / API Service - 'University API stores data in own DB' (landing store, versioning, receipt)
pipelineStages.whatPortalShows: Journey step 'Stored and acknowledged': stored-at, submission version number (v1, v2 resubmission ...), supersedes-submission link, duplicate detection result (same hash already stored), record count persisted, Receipt issued (receipt ID, hash, downloadable PDF/JSON). Resubmission history timeline per dataset x period lives here.

pipelineStages.system: Qlik Data Quality layer (inside Azure) - rule-based validation against the HEDB Data Dictionary (mandatory, coded lists, numeric limits, text length, cross-field, dates, primary-key duplicates)
pipelineStages.whatPortalShows: Journey step 'Validation': rule pack / dictionary version applied, started/finished, counts by severity (error | warning | info), pass rate, and the full ValidationIssue list (rule ID, field, row/key, actual value, expected, severity, message, EN/AR). Actions: download issue report (xlsx), open remediation, mark as acknowledged, request waiver for a rule. Outcome drives dataset status 'needs correction' vs proceed.

pipelineStages.system: Qlik Data Quality layer - statistical profiling of the submitted dataset
pipelineStages.whatPortalShows: Journey step 'Profiling': per-field completeness %, distinct counts, min/max/mean for numerics, code-list coverage (values not in the 44 referenced code lists), null pattern, and comparison to the institution's previous period (row-count delta, outlier flags). Presented as a profile card grid plus a 'what changed since last period' panel. KHDA Data can flag an anomaly for follow-up.

pipelineStages.system: Qlik Data Quality layer - transformation, standardisation, load to SaaS platform (Snowflake / SaaS data warehouse) and reference-data reconciliation with On-Prem School System (MSSQL) via Qlik data access
pipelineStages.whatPortalShows: Journey step 'Processing and acceptance': processing started/finished, reference-data reconciliation result, KHDA Data review decision (accept | return with comments), accepted-at, accepted-by, warehouse load timestamp. This is where dataset status becomes 'accepted'. Also shows hold reasons when KHDA Data pauses processing.

pipelineStages.system: Qlik Portal - real-time dashboards, KPIs and metrics, self-service reporting (the web application we are building, surfaced to the three roles)
pipelineStages.whatPortalShows: Journey step 'Published': dashboards refreshed-at, which KPIs/tiles include this submission, link to the institution's own dashboard and to KHDA sector dashboards. Portal-wide: submission progress ring, compliance matrix 37x46, compliance history (Required / Late / Missing / On-time computed from the Requirement table), leaderboard score with corrected formula, self-service report builder, exports/board packs.

securityObjects.ownerRole: KHDA IT issues and owns; Institution Admin views; one per institution per environment (sandbox, production)
securityObjects.lifecycle: requested (by Institution Admin or created during onboarding wave) -> issued -> active -> suspended (KHDA IT, e.g. security incident or offboarding) -> revoked. Never edited in place; a new client ID is issued instead.
securityObjects.portalSurface: KHDA IT > Institutions > [Institution] > Credentials tab (issue, suspend, revoke, view usage); Institution > Integration > API Credentials (read-only ID, environment, status, last used); Submission journey step 1 shows the client ID used.

securityObjects.ownerRole: KHDA IT generates; Institution Admin holds the value (shown once); KHDA IT sets expiry policy
securityObjects.lifecycle: generated (reveal-once modal, copy + download) -> active -> rotation started (new secret issued, old secret valid during grace window, e.g. 7 days as an illustrative default) -> old secret expired -> revoked. Expiry reminders at configurable lead times.
securityObjects.portalSurface: KHDA IT > Credentials (generate, rotate, set expiry, force-revoke; maker-checker approval on revoke in production); Institution > Integration > API Credentials (rotate self-service, expiry countdown, 'reveal once' banner); Notifications feed for expiring secrets; Audit trail for every generate/rotate/revoke.

securityObjects.object: Key pair (institution private key / registered public key)
securityObjects.ownerRole: Institution Admin generates the pair and keeps the private key; uploads the public key; KHDA IT registers/approves it on the API Hub
securityObjects.lifecycle: pending_upload -> uploaded (fingerprint computed) -> pending_approval (KHDA IT) -> registered/active -> expiring (notification) -> rotated (new key registered, old kept for overlap) -> revoked. Private key never leaves the institution and is never displayed in the portal.
securityObjects.portalSurface: Institution > Integration > Keys (upload public key PEM, view fingerprint, valid-from/to, rotate, download KHDA public key for response verification); KHDA IT > Credentials > Key approvals queue; Submission journey step 1 shows the key fingerprint used for signing.

securityObjects.ownerRole: Institution Admin requests; KHDA IT approves and applies at iPaaS and API Hub; scoped per environment
securityObjects.lifecycle: requested (IP or CIDR, label, environment, justification) -> pending_approval -> approved/active (applied to iPaaS and API Hub) -> rejected (with reason) -> removal_requested -> removed. Each entry records last-seen traffic so stale entries can be pruned.
securityObjects.portalSurface: Institution > Integration > IP Allowlist (table: IP/CIDR, label, environment, status, requested-by, approved-by, last seen; add/remove request); KHDA IT > Allowlist approvals (approve/reject with comment, bulk apply by wave); Integration Health shows rejected-by-IP events with the offending IP.

securityObjects.ownerRole: System-issued at runtime by iPaaS / API Hub; policy owned by KHDA IT; institution sees its own token activity
securityObjects.lifecycle: issued (client credentials or signed assertion) -> active (short-lived, expiry configured by KHDA IT) -> expired -> revoked (all tokens for a client on suspend/revoke). Tokens are never stored or displayed in full; only token ID, issued-at, expires-at, scope.
securityObjects.portalSurface: KHDA IT > Integration Health > Token activity (issuance timeline, failures by reason, per client); Institution > Integration > Activity log (my recent token issues/failures, self-diagnostics); Submission journey step 2 'token validated'.

securityObjects.ownerRole: KHDA IT enables per institution as part of onboarding touchpoints; Institution Admin runs connectivity tests
securityObjects.lifecycle: sandbox_enabled -> connectivity_test_passed (ping + sample submission) -> production_requested -> production_enabled -> production_suspended. Onboarding touchpoints reference these transitions.
securityObjects.portalSurface: KHDA IT > Institutions > Onboarding journey (touchpoints with real owners and dates); Institution > Integration > Environments (sandbox status, 'Run connectivity test', production go-live status); API docs and sandbox 'try it' console.

securityObjects.object: Portal user identity (UAE PASS for institutions, Active Directory for KHDA staff) and role assignment
securityObjects.ownerRole: Institution Admin invites and assigns institution sub-roles; KHDA IT manages KHDA staff access and can deactivate any user; KHDA Data has no user-admin rights
securityObjects.lifecycle: invited -> activated (first SSO sign-in) -> active -> role_changed -> deactivated. Approver and Steward must be different users (maker-checker constraint).
securityObjects.portalSurface: Institution > Settings > Users and roles; KHDA IT > Access management (all users, roles, last sign-in, deactivate); Audit trail entries for every role change; sign-in page with institution picker, UAE PASS, AD.

securityObjects.object: Channel exception (portal-upload waiver) and other waivers
securityObjects.ownerRole: Institution Admin requests; KHDA Data approves (policy) with KHDA IT informed for channel exceptions
securityObjects.lifecycle: requested -> under_review -> approved (with validity period, e.g. one reporting period as an illustrative default) -> expired -> revoked / rejected. Approved channel exception unlocks the Excel/portal upload bridge for that institution.
securityObjects.portalSurface: Institution > Requests > Waivers (new request, status, validity); KHDA Data > Waivers queue (approve/reject, comment); Dataset catalogue shows 'Upload enabled via exception until <date>'.

portalRequirements: Submission journey tracker: every Submission shows the pipeline stages (Source -> iPaaS -> API Hub -> Adapter -> Validation -> Profiling -> Processing -> Published) as a horizontal stepper with per-stage state, timestamps, correlation/request IDs, failure reason codes and a 'fix it' link; expandable stage detail panels.

Working actions, not stubs: portal upload (for exception-approved institutions), form entry, email/in-app notification sending, API docs, sandbox try-it console, exports - every button in the plan performs its action or shows an honest disabled reason.

Requirement table as the compliance backbone: one Requirement row per Institution x Dataset x Period (37 x 46 = 1,702 per period) with due date, applicability and waiver link; compliance history computes Required / Submitted / Late / Missing / On-time from it.

Corrected readiness score: denominators are required datasets (not submitted ones); timeliness rewards on-time and penalises lateness proportionally; datasets without due dates are excluded from the timeliness denominator; automation = API-channel accepted / required; ties broken by earlier acceptance not institution code; formula panel shows every input.

Validation detail: ValidationIssue list per submission with rule, field, row/key, value, expected, severity, EN/AR message; downloadable issue workbook; remediation queue grouped by dataset and rule; resubmission creates a new Submission version linked to the previous one.
Profiling report per submission: field completeness, code-list coverage, distributions, period-over-period deltas and anomaly flags visible to Institution and KHDA Data.

Maker-checker approvals: Steward prepares, Approver signs off before dispatch (institution side); KHDA Data accepts or returns after processing; KHDA IT credential revocations in production require a second approver; Approval entity records every decision.

Credential management as first-class objects: client ID, secret (reveal once, rotate with grace window, expiry countdown), key pair (public-key upload, fingerprint, rotation), IP allowlist (request -> approve -> apply), environment binding (sandbox -> production), with lifecycle states and audit entries.

Integration health for KHDA IT: per-institution and sector-wide auth success rate, IP rejections, token failures, gateway latency, throttling, last successful call, adapter persist failures, DQ queue depth; alerts with escalation.

Onboarding journey with real touchpoints: each institution shows touchpoints (kick-off, credentials issued, sandbox connected, sample submission validated, production enabled, first accepted submission) with owner, date, status; wave overview (Pilot Wave 1: 7, Wave 2: 14, Wave 3: 13, Wave 4: 3).

Compliance matrix 37 x 46 per period with status legend (non-submitted, processing, needs correction, accepted), filters by wave / subject area / frequency, click-through to the institution dataset agenda drawer.

Dictionary and schema versioning: DictionaryVersion entity (e.g. HEDB 2026, 2027) with effective periods; datasets and fields reference a version; every submission records the version validated against; diff view between versions; all 46 datasets including the 15 real-time ones carry EN/AR display names (no raw codes leaking).

Waiver / exception workflow: channel exception (portal upload), deadline extension, dataset not applicable, rule waiver - each with request, review, approval, validity and audit; approved waivers change how Requirement and Score treat the dataset.

Notifications feed and delivery: in-app feed per user, email with branded preview that actually sends, digest options, escalation engine (e.g. overdue 7 days -> Institution Admin, 14 days -> KHDA Data lead; illustrative thresholds), read/unread and links to the object.
Immutable audit trail: AuditEvent for every submission, approval, credential, allowlist, waiver, role change and dictionary change, filterable by institution, actor, object type, date; exportable.
Receipts: signed acknowledgment per stored submission (receipt ID, hash, timestamp, version) downloadable as PDF/JSON, referenced in the journey tracker and in compliance history.

Role-scoped navigation: Institution (Admin, Data Steward, Approver, Read-only), KHDA Data, KHDA IT; every page belongs to one role or is shared; row-level scoping so institutions only see their own data.
English and Arabic with full RTL, accessibility panel (page size, contrast, spacing, underline links, reduce motion), keyboard focus management - carried forward from the existing wireframe engine.
Metadata-driven engine carried forward: forms, validation, grid, Excel template, report and charts derived from dataset/field metadata; a dictionary update is a data change, not a code change.

Global search (institutions, datasets, submissions, receipts, users), saved views on catalogue/matrix/monitor, exports and board packs (xlsx/pdf), self-service report builder on the Qlik Portal surface.
Honest empty states and illustrative data labelling: any example numbers in mockups are marked as examples; unavailable metrics show why and what unlocks them.

institution: Institution Admin: manage institution profile and contacts; invite users and assign sub-roles (Steward, Approver, Read-only); request and hold API credentials (client ID, secret rotation, key pair upload); request IP allowlist entries; run sandbox connectivity tests; request waivers (channel exception, deadline extension, not applicable); view audit trail for the institution.

Data Steward: prepare submissions per dataset and period (API dispatch from source system, or form entry / Excel upload when a channel exception is approved); download Excel templates; review validation issues and fix data; resubmit new versions; monitor the submission journey; respond to KHDA Data follow-ups.
Approver: sign off Steward-prepared submissions before dispatch (maker-checker); approve resubmissions; acknowledge returned submissions; cannot be the same user as the Steward on a given submission.
Read-only: view dashboards, catalogue status, compliance history, leaderboard position, receipts and notifications without editing.

All institution roles: view their own dataset agenda (upcoming, overdue, real-time), submission progress, DQ score and readiness breakdown, notifications, receipts, dictionary specification per dataset, API docs and their own integration activity log.
khdaData: Monitor submissions across 37 institutions x 46 datasets per period: KHDA home KPIs, compliance matrix, monitor cards by wave, per-institution dataset agenda drawer.
Review data quality outputs: validation issue summaries, profiling anomalies, DQ score per institution and dataset; accept or return submissions after processing (KHDA acceptance decision).
Manage follow-up: send notifications and emails (with branded preview), set next steps and contacts, run escalation, log compliance history (Required / Late / Missing / On-time).

Manage the HEDB data dictionary: dataset and field definitions, code lists, display names EN/AR, dictionary versions and effective periods, validation rules; publish a new version without code change.
Manage reporting periods and requirements: open/close periods, set due dates per dataset frequency, mark applicability, approve waivers (channel exception, extension, not applicable, rule waiver).
Analytics and reporting: sector dashboards, leaderboard and score formulas, self-service reports, exports and board packs; validate that the score model uses required datasets as denominators.
khdaIt: Onboard institutions to the API by wave: track onboarding touchpoints with owners and dates; enable sandbox and production environments; publish API docs and sandbox try-it console.
Issue and manage credentials: client IDs, client secrets (generate, rotate, expire, revoke with second-approver in production), register institution public keys, publish KHDA public key.
Manage IP allowlists: approve or reject requests, apply to iPaaS and API Hub per environment, prune stale entries using last-seen data.

Watch pipeline and integration health: auth success rate, IP rejections, token failures, gateway latency and throttling, adapter persist failures, DQ queue depth; configure alerts and escalations; investigate a submission by correlation ID.
Security and access: manage KHDA staff access (Active Directory), deactivate any user, review audit trail, respond to incidents (suspend client, revoke tokens), maintain environment configuration.
Change and release: schedule maintenance windows, announce API version changes, coordinate dictionary version rollouts with KHDA Data, monitor legacy School System Portal usage.
